items.title: gateway: TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget is red on main (turn makes 19 of 30 images)
items.body:
TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget (internal/gateway, codex_images_test.go:359) fails standalone on current main 2374ffe1, macOS darwin/arm64, sandbox HOME with pinned caches:

    --- FAIL: TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget (0.02s)
        codex_images_test.go:359: turn 2 made 19 of 30 images, with 10 kept
        codex_images_test.go:359: turn 3 made 19 of 30 images, with 10 kept
    FAIL

Reproduce: `go test ./internal/gateway/ -run '^TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget$' -count=1` at 2374ffe1 (fetched today). It also went red under a full `go test -tags nogui ./...` run. Failing the same on main and not caused by the in-flight library PR; filing per 'a red gets its own issue' so it has an owner.

items.title: TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget is red on go1.27.3: turn 3 makes 19 of 30, one image fewer kept than the budget says
items.body:
On go1.27.3 (linux/amd64, a WSL2 dev box), on current main, run calmly on
its own:

    go test -tags nogui -run 'TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget' ./internal/gateway/

is red:

    codex_images_test.go:362: turn 3 made 19 of 30 images, with 10 kept

(expected: turn 1 makes 30, later turns 20, 10 kept). The test builds its
budget from the size of one fitted image (10*one+one/2), so anything that
changes image/png's encoder output size between Go versions shifts the
boundary and keeps one image fewer. CI stays green on 1.26.x; a 1.27 box
gets this deterministically.

Not tried: pinning Go 1.26 on the same box to confirm the encoder drift, or
printing the fitted sizes per turn.

items.title: bug(routing): Codex compaction can reclassify an unchanged native turn when transcript identity changes
items.body:
## Problem

An ongoing Codex task can be classified again after context compaction even though its native turn ID has not changed and no new task was submitted. This adds a classifier call and can make the route depend on the summary instead of the original task.

Observed on v0.1.1330. In one correlated routing/session trace, the parsed route turn changed from 7 to 1 immediately after compaction; a fresh classification appeared for the same native turn. The chosen model happened to stay the same, so this is evidence of duplicate classification, not proof of a model switch or measured monetary loss. No complete production HTTP payload was retained.

## Relevant implementation

At v0.1.1330 (`e00fbdbbc74f9829027a78769cbeb265d6271fb4`), `internal/gateway/rules.go` keys the turn decision by group, conversation identity and `firstWords(req)`, and determines continuation through `turnIn(req)`. Compaction can replace the first user text and renumber the parsed transcript. The v0.1.1363 source inspected also retains this key structure; that release has not been runtime-tested for this report.

## Minimal synthetic reproduction

Use local classifier/provider stubs and the Responses gateway with a Codex client user-agent:

1. Submit a user task with `client_metadata.thread_id="session-a"` and `turn_id="turn-a"` (or the corresponding supported transport metadata). Expect one classifier call.
2. Submit a replacement compacted transcript with different first user text, keeping the same session and native turn. No new task was issued. The current behavior classifies again; expected behavior is to preserve the active turn's decision.
3. Change the native turn to `turn-b`. This must classify again.
4. Also test a genuine native cross-thread delegation arriving inside the same active native turn: it must still establish a new task, rather than being suppressed by session/turn stickiness.

Steps 1–3 were reproduced through the actual gateway handler with loopback stubs. A negative control removing the proposed native-identity hookup makes the compaction assertion fail; restoring it passes. These are protocol-shaped tests, not byte-for-byte production replay.

## Proposed minimal repair (local prototype, not deployed)

- Where supported native metadata exists, bind classification continuity to group + session + native turn (and installation identity when available), rather than mutable transcript first words/parsed turn count.
- Preserve reclassification for a genuine new delegation within an active native turn. Our middleware already exposes the delegation text for classification; a boundary identity distinguishes a new dispatch from its tool continuations.
- Keep legacy behavior for clients without sufficient native identity; exclude prediction/title/description helpers from this binding.
- Preserve existing expiry, rule applicability and capacity checks. Do not pin a model for an entire session or change effort/provider selection.
- Store bounded identity digests, not raw task text, in the continuity state.

This is a repair proposal, not a claim that the prototype is production-ready. Middleware alone cannot reliably control the native classifier cache. Any upstream implementation should also preserve legitimate steering/new-task boundaries and existing concurrency behavior.

## Validation and limits

Local prototype based on v0.1.1330:

- Targeted native-turn, routing, Jev and middleware tests pass with `-race`; `go vet` and diff whitespace checks pass.
- Tests cover compaction continuation, a new native turn, new delegation within a turn, separate sessions, legacy fallback, and removing temporary middleware routing items before provider forwarding.
- Plain full gateway suite completed on both pristine base and patched source: 401.368s and 404.226s. Both fail the same tests: `TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget` (19/30 images with 10 kept), `TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON`, and `FuzzMarshalRaw/seed#7` (U+2028/U+2029 escaping). This is not a full-suite PASS. The image test also has a prior report in #2606.
- Full-package race runs were time-limited and did not complete; targeted race success is not full-package race coverage.
- All validation backends were local stand-ins. No real classifier/model requests or review reruns were made for these tests; no production binary/configuration was replaced.

This report intentionally omits account information, real task text, session IDs, local paths and private logs. Would you prefer a standalone regression test or a minimal patch for review?

items.title: routing: Free first silently spends In order when no member's cost is known (patch ready)
items.body:
# Free first silently spends In order when no member's cost is known (patch ready)

A pool routed `free` whose vendors' model lists nothing has fetched — and
whose models no catalog prices — has every seat judged paid. `FreeModel`
answers `false` for *this costs money* and for *nothing says what this costs*
alike, so `FreeFirst` returns the listed order and the pool spends **In
order** while reading as if it saved credits. A provider added a minute ago
is in exactly that state, so the routing can be set, look right in the
picker, and quietly do nothing at all.

Patch: **`keeuu/magpie` @ `pr/free-first-unknown`** — one commit on current
`main` (`635d6024`). This repo is `collaborators_only` for PRs, so here it
is as an issue with the branch to pull, as #3054 was.

## Reproduction

Two vendors, one served free and one served at a price, neither with a list
fetched yet. The paid one is listed first:

```
magpie provider add freev url=http://127.0.0.1:3491/v1 key=sk-free models=m
magpie provider add paidv url=http://127.0.0.1:3492/v1 key=sk-paid models=m
magpie group add G models=paidv/m,freev/m routing=free
```

| vendor list | served by | `freev` hits | `paidv` hits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| not fetched | `paidv` | 0 | **1** |
| fetched (`freev` marks `m` free) | `freev` | **1** | 0 |

The trace agrees with the first row — every seat reads `free=false`, which is
also what a pool where every model is genuinely paid reads:

```
order: [(paidv, False), (freev, False)]
```

## Root cause

`internal/provider/models.go`, `FreeModel`:

```go
pr, ok := p.ListPrice(model)
return ok && pr.Input == 0 && ... // ok is false with no list and no price
```

With no live list `Available()` is empty; with no catalog entry `ListPrice`
finds nothing. Both "priced" and "unknown" land on `false`.

## The patch

`provider.FreeModelKnown(model) (free, known bool)` tells the two apart:
`false, false` is unknown, not paid. `FreeModel` keeps its signature and its
answers — `free, _ := FreeModelKnown(model); return free` — so nothing else
that reads it changes.

`weighRouted` reads it and records `freeUnknown` when **no** seat could be
told free or paid; `GroupRef` carries that to the trace (`freeUnknown`), and
the Routing page says the request went in the listed order because no cost is
known yet.

```
docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md            |   2 +-
internal/gateway/fallback.go                  |   2 +
internal/gateway/freefirst_nofree_test.go     | 166 ++++++++++++++++++
internal/gateway/gateway.go                   |   1 +
internal/gateway/routing.go                   |  14 ++-
internal/gateway/trace.go                     |  10 ++
internal/gui/assets/plugins/routing/client.js |   3 +
internal/provider/freemodel_test.go           |  89 ++++++++++
internal/provider/models.go                   |  24 +++-
```

## What it deliberately stays quiet about

A pool where every model **is** known paid stays silent. There the user asked
for free first, nothing is free, and spending In order is the routing working
as intended; a "can't tell" warning would be a false alarm. Only the state
where **no** seat could be judged at all is reported.

`TestFreeFirstIsQuietWhenEveryMemberIsKnownPaid` exists to hold that line.

## Verification

**Broken by hand both ways, at the patch's head:**

- `freeUnknown` forced to `false` → `TestFreeFirstSaysWhenNoMemberCostIsKnown`
  goes red: *"free first ordered nothing and the trace doesn't say so"*.
- `freeUnknown` set whenever no seat is free (ignoring `known`) →
  `TestFreeFirstIsQuietWhenEveryMemberIsKnownPaid` goes red: *"both costs were
  known and paid; the routing worked, so nothing is unknown"*.

Restored, both green.

**At the patch's head, rebased onto current `main`:**

- `gofmt -l internal/provider internal/gateway internal/gui`: clean.
- `go vet ./internal/provider ./internal/gateway`: clean.
- `go test ./internal/provider -count=1`: ok (53s).
- `go test ./internal/routes -count=1`: ok.
- `go test ./internal/gateway -run TestFreeFirst -count=1`: ok, including the
  three new ones.
- `go test ./internal/gui -run TestCoreScriptBudget`: ok.
- `node --test internal/gui/tests/i18n-keys.test.cjs`: 3/3 pass.

Full `./internal/gateway -count=1` leaves one red,
`TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget` (`turn 2 made 19 of 30 images, with 10
kept`). It fails on `main` without this patch too — checked with the branch
stashed — so it is not part of this change.

## Not in the patch, for you to decide

The new hint is **English only**. `zh`, `zh-TW`, `ja` and `de` are left out so
the wording can settle first; `i18n-keys` does not require a translation to
exist, so nothing goes red meanwhile. Both the wording and the four languages
are yours to pick — say the word and I'll put them in.

## Files worth a look

- `internal/provider/models.go` — `FreeModelKnown`, and `FreeModel` on top of
  it.
- `internal/gateway/routing.go` — where `freeUnknown` is decided.
- `internal/gateway/freefirst_nofree_test.go` — the three cases, including
  `pricedInCatalog`, a helper for the state `liveModels` cannot express (a
  vendor's list says whether a model is free, never what it costs).

items.title: [bug] sessions: a Claude Code fork subagent's copy of its parent's reply is counted twice (branch ready; PRs are collaborators-only)
items.body:
Branch: [fish2lab/magpie `sessions-claude-fork-copy`](https://github.com/fish2lab/magpie/tree/sessions-claude-fork-copy), one commit, [df11f97](https://github.com/fish2lab/magpie/commit/df11f97d0e16279d889b0f0da8a353b6d903661d), on origin/main 7d075df. I'm filing it as an issue because PRs here are limited to collaborators.

```
git fetch https://github.com/fish2lab/magpie sessions-claude-fork-copy && git cherry-pick df11f97
```

## What's wrong

A Claude Code fork subagent's transcript (`<session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`, here from Claude Code 2.1.302) opens with a `fork-context-ref` line. Next comes a copy of the parent's reply that started the fork, with the same `message.id` and `requestId`, now marked `isSidechain: true` with the fork's `agentId`. Then comes the fork's own prompt. The parent's main file already counts that reply, and the sessions reader dedupes calls only within a file. So `magpie sessions` and the stats count the reply once more for every fork.

## The fix

Subsystem: sessions (`internal/sessions`, the Claude Code reader). No subsystem reference documents how Claude transcripts are counted, so no page changes.

- Trigger: a `fork-context-ref` line. The reader sets `state.ForkHead` and skips assistant lines until the file's first user line. It does this both in the fast path (`claudeLine`) and in the full parse (`claudeFull`). The first user line clears the flag, and everything after it is counted as before.
- Before: the copied reply counted once in the parent's file and again in each fork's file. After: it counts once, in the parent's file.
- State: `ForkHead` is kept in the parse cache (`fork_head`), so a read that resumes inside the head still skips. `cacheVersion` goes from 22 to 23, so files parsed before are read again.
- Files without a `fork-context-ref` line read as before. These include ordinary subagents, workflow agents and main transcripts.

## Verification

Run at df11f97 (on origin/main 7d075df), go1.27.3 darwin/arm64:

- `gofmt -l` is clean.
- Vet is clean: `go vet ./...`, `GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui ./...` and `GOOS=windows go vet ./...`.
- Builds are ok: `go build`, `GOOS=linux go build -tags nogui` and `GOOS=windows go build`.
- `go test -tags nogui -count=1 ./...` in a sandbox HOME with Go's caches pinned: 69 packages ok, including `internal/sessions` (ok, 73s). A few packages are red, and they are red in the same way on origin/main 7d075df without this change:
  - `internal/provider`: #3632 (ok in 71s with `TestUnreadLoginsWriteErrorsKeepCredentials` skipped)
  - `internal/gateway`: `TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON` and `FuzzMarshalRaw` (#3547), `TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget` (#3549), `TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback` (#3680)
  - `internal/plugin`: `TestPluginSOCKSProxy` (#2207)
- Broken by hand: I put the old `claude.go` and `sessions.go` back and kept the new test. `TestClaudeForkSubagentCountsParentReplyOnce` then fails with `session: {Input:250 Output:25 CacheRead:30 ...}, want {Input:150 Output:15 CacheRead:20 ...}`. With the change restored, it passes.

I also checked against real data. I copied one real session (its main file and its one fork) into a sandbox, with HOME, the XDG dirs and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` all pointing there, and ran `magpie sessions --json` with binaries built from origin/main and from this branch:

| | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| input | 238 | 236 |
| output | 153,562 | 150,944 |
| cache read | 24,171,440 | 24,041,229 |
| cache write | 388,781 | 387,933 |

The branch's numbers equal that session's calls deduped by `message.id` + `requestId` across all of its files, as counted by an independent reader, [git-tab](https://github.com/fish2lab/git-tab)'s Claude Code adapter.

Not tried:

- Cowork transcripts, which use the same reader.
- Running on Linux or Windows; only the GOOS vet and builds above were run. The change has no platform code.

## Found while checking, not changed here

I compared 115 sessions from the last 30 days against git-tab, and 100 matched to the cent. Three other differences come from magpie behavior I left alone. I can open a separate issue for any of them if useful:

- `sessions` and the stats price each model's total at its base tier (`p.At(0)` in `sessions.go` and `stats.go`). So Claude Haiku 5.5's rate for prompts above 100K tokens ($0.50/$2.50 per MTok, against $0.10/$0.50) is never applied. One pi session on Haiku 5.5 had identical tokens on both sides. It cost $0.12 in magpie, against $0.52 when each request is priced at its tier.
- DeepSeek's peak-hour price is not applied. It is 2× on weekdays 9:00–12:00 and 14:00–18:00 Beijing time ([pricing page](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/quick_start/pricing)). Two pi sessions on deepseek-flash that ran entirely in peak hours came out at half their price.
- A forked or resumed Claude Code session copies its parent's history into a new main file under a new `sessionId`. Per-session totals then count the copied calls in both sessions. In one fork the copies made up 95% of its listed cost: $6.62 listed, against $0.31 for its own calls.

items.title: library: 安装 market skill 时，超过 8 MiB 的 Git tree 被截断并报 JSON 错误
items.body:
## 问题概述

Magpie macOS 桌面版 `0.1.1285` 无法通过“资源库 → 技能 → 发现”从 `sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills` 添加 `clean-code`。

问题不在于所选的 `SKILL.md` 文件过大：`skills/clean-code/SKILL.md` 本身很小。安装器在安装单个 Skill 前，会先下载并解析**整个仓库**的递归 Git tree；该响应超过了 Magpie 的本地读取上限。

配置 GitHub token 后，Magpie 显示：

```text
GitHub's list of sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills's files wasn't understood: unexpected end of JSON input
```

## 复现步骤

1. 打开“资源库 → 技能 → 发现”，搜索 `clean`。
2. 在“设置 → 网络与共享”中配置 GitHub token。
3. 点击 `sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills` 中 `clean-code` 的“添加”。

### 实际结果

按钮显示“保存中…”约五秒，随后报出上述错误；Skill 未被加入资源库。

### 预期结果

Magpie 应能安装选中的 `clean-code` 目录，而不需要先加载这个大型仓库完整的递归文件列表。

## 已验证的尺寸边界

我通过已认证的 GitHub REST API 请求了 Magpie 使用的同一端点：

```text
GET /repos/sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills/git/trees/HEAD?recursive=1
```

结果如下：

- 响应大小：**11,267,651 bytes**（约 **10.75 MiB**）
- tree 条目数：**39,614**
- GitHub 返回：`"truncated": false`

当前主分支中，通用 `apiGet` 通过 `io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 8<<20)` 将响应读取限制为 **8,388,608 bytes（8 MiB）**，随后再执行 `json.Unmarshal`。因此这个合法的 11.27 MB JSON 响应会先在 Magpie 本地被截断，再被 JSON 解码器报告为 `unexpected end of JSON input`，与界面中的错误完全吻合。

我还在同一个 Magpie 进程中删除并成功重新添加了 `wondelai/skills` 的 `clean-architecture`，说明资源库并非整体无法安装。未配置 token 时出现的是预期的匿名 GitHub API 限额错误；配置 token 后才稳定复现这里的 JSON 错误。

## 与 #1941 及仓库增长的关系

这不是 [#1941](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/1941) 中“仓库解压后超过 200 MB”限制重新出现，也不是所选 Skill 的内容过大。

- `apiGet` 的通用 **8 MiB** 上限在 2026-10-06 引入，当时主要用于较小的 GitHub API 响应。
- #1941 的回退路径在 2026-10-13 上线：当完整仓库下载超过 200 MB 时，`fetchSkillFiles` 会调用 `repoTree`，从 `git/trees?recursive=1` 取得完整文件列表，再仅下载各 Skill 目录的文件。
- 这条新回退路径复用了 `apiGet`，于是把可能大于 8 MiB 的完整 tree 响应放进了原先的通用上限；`tree.Truncated` 的处理也在 JSON 解析之后，因此到不了。

对同一 Git tree 端点按历史提交抽样，响应体已在 #1941 上线前越过 8 MiB：

| 日期（UTC） | 响应大小 |
| --- | ---: |
| 2026-07-01 | 7,336,178 bytes（约 7.00 MiB） |
| 2026-08-01 | 8,517,622 bytes（约 8.12 MiB） |
| 2026-09-01 | 9,136,851 bytes（约 8.71 MiB） |
| 2026-10-18 | 11,267,651 bytes（约 10.75 MiB） |

因此，`agentic-awesome-skills` 的快速增长是触发条件，但不是仓库作者的错误：该 tree 在回退路径被引入前已经超过 8 MiB。问题在于回退路径没有为合法的大型 tree 响应设置独立且可检测的边界。

## 建议的修复方向

建议分两部分处理：

1. **不要解析被静默截断的响应。** 对 Git tree 响应使用独立、可配置且有界的上限（至少覆盖本例的 11.27 MB）；读取至多 `limit + 1` bytes，超过上限时返回明确的、带类型的“Git tree 响应过大”错误，并处理 `ReadAll` 的读取错误。诊断信息可包含端点与上限，但不应包含 token。
2. **长期按所选目录获取。** #1941 当前需要完整 tree 来发现其中的 Skill 目录。若 market 条目能够携带，或首次探测后记录所选 Skill 的仓库相对路径，安装单个 Skill 时就可以只列举并下载该目录，避免为单个 Skill 枚举完整仓库。

单纯提高通用 8 MiB 上限可以临时修复本仓库，但更大的仓库仍会遇到同类问题。

## 建议补充的回归测试

- 合法的递归 tree 响应超过 8 MiB 时，不能再表现为 JSON 语法错误。
- `sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills` 的 `clean-code` 能成功安装。
- 真正超出新上限时，错误应说明尺寸边界且不泄露凭据。
- 若实现路径级获取，仓库完整 tree 很大时，只请求所选 Skill 目录。

items.title: Routing can only be watched in the magpie that serves the gateway, and that magpie changes by itself
items.body:
**What happens**

Two magpie instances run on one Mac: the app (menu bar, opens at login) and
`magpie web --addr <tailscale name>:3430`, so a second Mac can open its page.

Only one of them can hold `127.0.0.1:3425`. Whichever binds it first serves the
gateway; the other is its client; when the serving one exits, the other takes
over. magpie says this itself:

> "the gateway on http://127.0.0.1:3425 is served by another magpie … this page shows the same settings and accounts, and serves the gateway once that one stops"

**The Routing page shows live routing only in the instance that holds 3425. The other shows none.**

**Reproduction:** run both instances, then **update magpie once** — the update
restarts whichever instance holds 3425 (the app's update restarts it; a service
is the `magpie daemon restart # after updating magpie` the reference names).
Once the takeover is over, the **new holder** shows live routing and the
**previous holder** (now a client) shows nothing.

So **which instance can show routing follows whoever holds 3425** — and with a
second instance on the same Mac, **every update causes it**.

Versions: app 0.1.1255 / `magpie web` 0.1.1238 (both stock builds).

**Why this feels inconsistent**

1. The single-writer rule explains who may **serve**: two at once would keep
   separate in-flight and accounting state (a takeover carries no state over;
   the new holder starts with none). It says nothing about who may **read**.
2. "The routing data is locked inside the serving process" does not hold:
   per-session routing is already an API — `GET /v1/magpie/route?session=<id>`
   (400 "name the session" without the parameter, 200 with it), which
   `magpie statusline` reads as a client to show where a turn went. What is
   locked is **that one live page**, not the data.
3. This would follow a pattern the reference already describes: with a Remote
   magpie provider, another machine's models, routing-group ids, and its
   accounts' usage and limits are shown here, and `GET /v1/magpie/limit`
   answers one key's own limits — *"it reads nothing from the request but its
   key"*. Publishing live routing the same way (loopback, read-only, minimal)
   would fit that pattern rather than introduce a new one. If there is a reason
   it should not be published that way, I would be glad to know it.
4. Two instances on one Mac is not an accident: magpie has a message for it
   (*"another magpie serves the gateway at …: set its port there, or quit it
   first"*), and `magpie web` steps aside when a service already serves the
   page. So the case is known: **the serving half is handled, the watching half
   is not.**

**What upstream itself says**

- `internal/gateway/gateway.go`: `Window says this process shows the routing of
  the gateway it serves`, and that `magpie serve` has none (#110).
- **#110** (closed): the same problem — with `magpie serve` serving the
  gateway, the Routing page said the routing "plays live in that magpie's
  window" while `serve` has no window, so it could be watched nowhere. It was
  closed by fixing the wording (that is today's "this page shows the same
  settings and accounts…"), so the state itself is still not shared.
- **#506**: why `ServedBy` asks who answers (an update left another magpie on
  the port, and an error worded as an older version misled two people) — the
  two-instance case is treated as something to report and quit, not to use.

**Proposal**

Publish the serving instance's routing state on loopback, in the shape
`/v1/magpie/limit` already uses (read-only, minimal, answers only what is
asked):

1. **Lanes need nothing new**: `GET /v1/magpie/concurrency` already answers
   each key's or account's lanes (this computer, or a gateway key when shared).
   What is missing is the aggregate live trace: please add `GET
   /v1/magpie/trace`, answering what `Server.Trace` holds (with `after` and
   `wait` for a long poll), on loopback alone — never on the shared listener.
   Reaching `http://<server>:3425/` from another machine already fails today,
   so keep it that way.
2. The instance that is not serving reads that and renders the same Routing
   page (it already has the page and the handlers); `/api/lanes` and the state
   read come from the serving magpie too.
3. The Routing page names the instance that is routing (app / `magpie web` /
   `serve` / `tui`, its pid and address), taken from the serving instance's own
   answer (`pid` and `serves` in `/`), so it follows a takeover by itself.
4. Serving and takeover behavior unchanged; nothing is written.

**If the current behavior is intended, a line in the reference on why would
help: it describes the behavior, but not the reason.**

**Diagram**

```
         ┌──── gateway (router+core, single writer) :3425 ────┐
         │ live routing/lanes live only in the holder's memory │
         │ proposal: read-only state plane (loopback)          │
         │   GET /v1/magpie/trace       (new · aggregate trace)│
         │   GET /v1/magpie/concurrency (exists · lanes)       │
         │   pid / serves in /          (new · identity)       │
         └──────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘
                            │ this computer, loopback, no key
                            ▼
         ┌──── the console of one that does not serve ──────────┐
         │ reads the state plane and renders the same Routing   │
         │ page, whose heading names who is routing (follows a  │
         │ takeover by itself) · read-only, nothing written     │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
(Today: only the instance that holds 3425 shows routing.)
```

**A patch for this is ready on a fork**: `fatcutegg/magpie`, one commit rebased
on today's `main` (built and tested there), so the compare page carries the
whole diff:
https://github.com/yetone/magpie/compare/main...fatcutegg:magpie:main?expand=1

Its description, its boundaries (loopback only, read-only, serving and takeover
unchanged) and what was run are in the commit message. This repository accepts
pull requests from collaborators only, so I could not open one: if you would
like to look at it as a pull request, invite me and I will open it; otherwise
the change can be taken from that compare page, or sent as a patch.

items.title: gateway: a Codex compaction cut on every candidate returns 502 instead of compacting locally
items.body:
## Summary

When Codex compaction goes through a single model with no remaining
fallback candidate, and every summary stream ends before its terminal
event, `codexCompact` returns `502` even though all candidates have
already been tried. Codex retries it three times, then Magpie's 5-minute
compaction guard answers `400`; the conversation cannot compact or
continue.

This is the remaining no-candidate case after #2274. It is not a
request-shape refusal such as #3106.

## Observed environment

- Magpie `v0.1.1327` on Windows (`magpie-windows-amd64.exe`).
- Codex using `openai_base_url = http://127.0.0.1:3425/backend-api/codex`.
- The conversation's model was the direct provider model
  `commandcode/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`; it was not a routing group
  and had no fallback model configured.
- Reasoning effort was `max`.
- The Command Code provider had two keys; Magpie tried both.

## Evidence

Three compaction requests returned `502` after about 150 seconds each.
The final UI error was:

```text
compaction: commandcode/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash failed to summarise this conversation 3 times in a row
(last: Command Code: the reply ended before it was complete)
```

The summary request was about 123,353 tokens; tool results were about
68,033 of them. Magpie's `usage.jsonl` records both Command Code keys
failing for the same conversation, so this is not one bad credential and
not a user-side download failure.

I checked the current `origin/main` at `7d67910f` (`v0.1.1438`): the
no-candidate behavior is still present. `askWhole` correctly holds the
summary until it ends, and `serve` correctly fails over candidates. Once
all candidates are exhausted, however, `codexCompact` omits this
cut-summary `502` from the existing plain-text/local fallback condition
and returns the `502` to Codex.

## Expected

A cut summary must never be reused as the summary. But once every
candidate has already failed with `the reply ended before it was
complete`, Magpie should make a local handoff summary and return a
successful compaction item, as it already does after the plain-text retry
fails for the 404/protection cases. The local summary already says it is
not a model summary and tells the next agent to inspect the workspace.

This avoids paying for the same large prompt three times while still
preserving the "never use partial output" rule.

## Proposed fix

In `codexCompact`, recognise the exact `errEndedShort` failure returned
from `serve` after candidate exhaustion and fall back to `localSummary`.
Do not treat a partial model reply as complete, and do not change the
handling of 401/403/429 or request-shape failures.

The regression test should use a single fake provider whose Responses
stream ends without `response.completed`. Before the fix it returns `502`;
after the fix it should return one Magpie compaction item containing the
local handoff, while never including the partial stream text. The existing
fallback test with a second working candidate must still use that
candidate's complete summary.

## Related

- #2274: added whole-summary holding, candidate failover, and the
  compaction guard. This issue covers the case left with nobody to fail
  over to.
- #3125: the same final error on `gpt-6.1-sol`; no comments or fix yet.
- #2790: Command Code compaction failure, but its last error is a Chat
  message-shape refusal rather than a cut stream.

## Verification plan

- Add a test that fails on `7d67910f` with `502`, then passes with the
  local handoff.
- Keep `TestCodexCompactCutSummaryFailsOver` green: a complete fallback
  summary still wins.
- Confirm the local summary excludes the partial words from the cut
  stream and records why compaction was local.
- Run the gateway compaction tests, the full Go suite under a sandboxed
  HOME, `go vet` for the required platforms, and the Windows build.

AI disclosure: investigated and drafted with AI assistance under the
reporter's direction; the claims above are backed by local Magpie usage
logs and the current `origin/main` source.

items.title: routing: Free first — spend a subscription's free models before the ones that spend its allowance (patch ready)
items.body:
**A working patch is ready.** The repo's `pull_request_creation_policy` is `collaborators_only`, so this comes as an issue with the branch linked rather than as a PR. Branch: https://github.com/keeuu/magpie/compare/main...keeuu:pr/free-first (4 commits, 22 files, 410 insertions), rebased onto `dee5c9d7`.

---

## Problem

A pool — a provider's accounts or keys, or a routing group's members — can be routed Smart, In order, In turn, Least used first, Weekly pace, By weight or Manual. None of them asks what a request **costs**. So a group that names a subscription's free model beside paid ones spends whichever the routing happens to pick first, and a model its vendor serves at no cost to the allowance can sit behind one that spends it until something fails.

Users notice this most on the groups `magpie` builds (`auto/<model>`), where one model is often served free by one subscription and at a price by another.

## Change (gateway routing, `internal/routes`)

Add a routing `free`, Free first: the seats whose model its vendor serves at no cost to the subscription's allowance or credits go first, in their listed order, and the rest after them, also in their listed order. A request therefore spends what costs nothing before it spends anything, and nothing that was free is left behind a paid seat.

- `routes.Seat` gains `Free`, and `routes.Strategy` gains `ByFree`.
- `routes.FreeFirst` sorts the two tiers and nothing else. Within a tier the listed order stands — a free seat is **not** pushed behind a paid one for running low, since a free seat spends nothing by running out.
- `weighRouted` fills `Seat.Free` from `provider.FreeModel` **only** when the serving strategy has `ByFree` set, so Smart, In order, In turn, Least used first, Weekly pace and By weight never read a model list for it and pay nothing for this.
- `provider.FreeModel` takes the vendor's own word (`catalog.Model.Free`: WorkBuddy's `x0.00`, Qoder's `is_free`/`price_factor` 0, Cline's free models, an OpenCode Zen free one), and otherwise a list price of $0 on every count, so a key's free model is spent first too.
- A model neither marked free nor priced at 0 is not free: a pool with no free model behaves exactly as In order, so setting the routing on such a group changes nothing.

Wired through every list a routing appears in: the two saving whitelists (`provider.Group`'s and `provider.Provider`'s, which reset an unknown routing to Smart's `""`), `plugins/rotation`'s `routes.Builtin`, `app.js`'s `ROUTINGS` and its `ROTATION` set, the Routing page's options, hints and trace explanations, the TUI's `routings`, and the CLI's `routingNames` (`free`, also `free-first`).

## Why not a plugin

`internal/routes` already has the point (`routes.Register`), and a JS gateway plugin's `strategies` could order a pool. A plugin cannot fill `Seat.Free`, though: `seatJSON` (`internal/middleware/points.go`) gives a strategy `key`, `account`, `known`, `learns`, `used`, `soon`, `pace`, `weight`, `resting` and `tokens` — nothing about the model's price, and nothing that names the provider or model behind a seat. A strategy that can't tell a free seat from a paid one can't implement this, so the flag has to come from the core, and once it is there the strategy belongs beside the others in `routes.Builtin`.

The flag is filled only when `Strategy.ByFree` is set, so nothing else pays for the model lists it reads.

## Acceptance criteria

Run at `c52e7f0c`, Go 1.27.3, macOS 26 arm64.

1. **A test that fails without the change.** `TestFreeFirstPutsFreeAheadOfPaid` — putting `FreeFirst`'s order back to `identity(len(seats))` (the change reverted, everything else in place) fails with `order = [0 1 2 3], want [1 3 0 2]` and `order = [0 1 2], want [2 0 1]`. Restored, both pass.
2. **Tests in a sandbox.** `go test -tags nogui ./...` under a temporary HOME with `GOPATH`/`GOMODCACHE`/`GOCACHE` pinned: 63 packages ok. Two failures are not this change's and are on `main` untouched:
   - `gateway.TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget` (`turn 2 made 19 of 30 images, with 10 kept`) — reproduced with `git stash -u` on the unmodified tree.
   - `gui.TestCoreScriptBudget` was this change's, fixed by the budget raise below.
3. **The build and the suite.** `gofmt -l` on the changed files prints nothing. `go vet ./...`, `GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui ./...`, `GOOS=windows go vet ./...` pass. `go build`, `GOOS=linux go build -tags nogui`, `GOOS=windows go build` pass. `go test -tags nogui ./...` as above.
4. **GUI tests in both engines.** `routing-save.test.cjs`, `builtins.test.cjs` and `routing-columns.test.cjs` pass on Chromium and WebKit, in English and Chinese, run serially (20/20; run concurrently, three of them contend for CPU and one timing assertion goes red, which is not this change). `strings.cjs` passes: the new strings have their Traditional Chinese, Japanese and German with the same placeholders.
5. **Real use.** Against a live gateway, a group `workbuddy/glm-5.3` (paid, first) + `opencode-zen-free/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` routed `free` answered from `opencode-zen-free` three times running, while the same members routed `order` answered from `workbuddy/glm-5.3` — the trace (`/v1/magpie/route`) names which. `workbuddy/deepseek-v4.1-flash` is the one member the vendor does not mark free in the group `auto/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, and it sorts behind the three that are.

Not run: native Windows and Linux execution. Cross-compilation is not runtime validation, and this change's only platform-specific code is none — the routing is platform-independent Go.

## How it works with Sink and rests

`free` decides **where a seat sits**; it does not decide what happens when a seat can't answer. That is already the gateway's own: a rate limited seat rests for as long as the vendor says (its `ResetsAt`), and `Sink` moves one rate limited with quota left to the back of its pool for the life of the process (`sink.go`, `Provider.Sink`). A group with `sink: true` routed `free` keeps both — the free band is the order the strategy gives, the sinking and resting happen around it, and neither fights the other: `goesRound("free")` is false, so `sinks` is on for it exactly as it is for Smart or In order.

The two answer different questions and neither replaces the other:

- **Sink / rest** — a seat that failed right now (429, out of quota) stops being tried until it recovers. This is the mechanism that keeps a free model's *vendor* rate limit from costing a request.
- **`free`** — a seat that costs nothing is tried before one that spends. This is what keeps an allowance from being spent while a free alternative sits behind it.

A pool can want both, and does: a group whose free members are one vendor's rate-limited free model and another's $0 model wants the free band tried first *and* the one that just took a 429 left out until it resets.

One thing this routing deliberately does **not** read is a seat's allowance share. Qoder CN's DeepSeek-Flash is free at `price_factor` 0 while the account's credits read 300/300 spent — those credits are the plan's, spent by other models, and the free model never draws on them. Sorting a free seat by the account's share would put the one seat that still answers behind ones that can't. So the free band keeps its listed order rather than Smart's tiers; what limits a free model is its vendor's rate limit, which a failure rests. This is why `FreeFirst` is one split and not a second Smart.


## Notes

`app.js` grows 1,195 bytes for the option's description, 195 over `appScriptBudget`. The description stays in the core because both the provider editor (`ROUTINGS`) and the Routing page's plugin (`routingOf`, `routingSegs`) read this one list; the budget is raised to 1,271,000 (1.5% over the measured 1,269,195), with what it is for said in the comment, as each raise before it did.

`routing-save`'s "every routing back" counts move from 5/6 to 6/7: with `plugins/rotation` on, an account's picker offers six routings (By weight is a provider's keys alone) and one with keys seven.

---

<details>
<summary>中文说明（给中文使用者）</summary>

**做了什么**：新增一种路由方式 `free`（免费优先）。供应商或路由组设成它以后，供应商**不消耗本订阅额度或积分**的模型排在前面，按原顺序尝试；这些都不能响应时，才轮到要花额度的。所以不花钱的一个都不会剩下。

**判定「免费」**：优先看供应商自己的标记（WorkBuddy 的 `x0.00`、Qoder 的 `is_free` / `price_factor` 为 0、Cline 和 OpenCode Zen 的免费模型），没有标记时看目录价是否四项全为 $0。都不是就不算免费——某个池子没有任何免费模型时，它的行为与「按顺序」完全一致。

**为什么不写成插件**：`routes` 的策略扩展点已经有了，JS 网关插件也能注册 `strategies`，但 `seatJSON` 交给策略的字段里没有「这个座位花不花钱」的信息，也没有供应商和模型名，插件拿不到这个判断依据。所以 `Free` 标记必须由核心填，策略也就放在 `routes.Builtin` 里最合适。

**开销**：只有设了 `Strategy.ByFree` 的策略才会去读模型列表，Smart、按顺序、轮流、最少使用、重置前用完、按权重这些完全不受影响、零额外开销。

**与限流的关系**：`free` 只决定「谁排前面」，不管「谁挂了怎么办」——后者本来就是网关自己的事：被限流的座位按供应商给的恢复时间休息（rest），`Sink` 把「限流但还有额度」的挪到池子队尾。组设了 `sink: true` 再加 `free` 路由时，两者同时生效、互不冲突（`goesRound("free")` 为 false，所以 `sinks` 照常开着）。简单说：**Sink 管「谁现在不能用了」，`free` 管「谁更便宜先用」**，一个问题不替代另一个。

**故意不读额度**：Qoder CN 的 DeepSeek-Flash 是 `price_factor` 0（免费），但账户 credits 显示 300/300 已用完——那些 credits 是套餐的，被别的模型花掉了，免费模型根本不消耗它。如果按账户额度排序，反而会把**唯一还能用的座位**排到不能用的人后面。所以免费档内保持原顺序，不套用 Smart 的分档。免费模型真正受限的是供应商限流，那由失败后的 rest 处理。这也是 `FreeFirst` 只做一次二分、而不是再造一个 Smart 的原因。

**验证**：对一个真实网关，`workbuddy/glm-5.3`（付费，排第一）+ `opencode-zen-free/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` 设成 `free` 时三次请求都走了免费那个；同样两个成员设成 `order` 时走的是付费那个。路由轨迹（`/v1/magpie/route`）能看出区别。

</details>

---

**If this belongs in magpie**, the branch above applies to `dee5c9d7` as a fast-forward; `git cherry-pick 970da789..c52e7f0c` on a fresh `main` is the same thing. I'll change anything in it — the routing's name, its place in the picker, whether it should weigh the paid tier by Smart instead of the listed order, the budget raise — to whatever the project prefers. If the idea is wanted but the implementation isn't, that's fine too.

I'm happy to move it to a PR the moment this account is a collaborator.
